name: Diagnostic_SEQ-SNF_1
questiontext: What is the sum to infinity of the geometric progression \({{CT:0}} + {{CT:1}} + {{CT:2}} + {{CT:3}} + \ldots\)? [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback: The sum to infinity \(S_{\infty}\) of a geometric progression, first term \(a\) and common ratio \(r\), is defined provided \(\mid r \mid<1\), in which case it is given by the equation \[ S_{\infty}=\frac{a}{1 - r}. \] Here \(a = {{CT:4}}\) and \(r = {{CT:5}}\) so \(S_{\infty} = {{CT:6}}\).

on_true.feedback: The sum to infinity of a geometric progression, first term \(a\) and common ratio \(r\), where \(\mid r \mid<1\), is \[\frac{a}{1-r}. \] Here \(a = {{CT:4}}\) and \(r = {{CT:5}}\). Your answer is \[\frac{a}{1+r}.\]

The sum to infinity of a geometric progression, first term \(a\) and common ratio \(r\), where \(\mid r \mid<1\), is \[\frac{a}{1-r}\mbox{.} \] Here \(a = {{CT:4}}\) and \(r = {{CT:5}}\). Your answer is \[\frac{ar}{1+r}\mbox{.}\]
